q: 1. Soil can exist in .............
explain: Depending on conditions, soil can be a three-phase system (solid-water-air), two-phase (dry solid-air, or saturated solid-water), or approach single-phase, so all apply.

q: 2. The relationship between void ratio (e) and porosity ratio (n) is:
explain: Since n = e/(1+e), rearranging gives e = n(1+e), the correct relation linking porosity and void ratio.

q: 3. The degree of saturation for fully saturated soil is .............
explain: A fully saturated soil has all void spaces filled with water, giving a degree of saturation of 1 (100%).

q: 4. The ratio of volume of voids to the total volume of the given soil mass is known as
explain: Porosity (n) is defined as the ratio of the volume of voids to the total (bulk) volume of the soil.

q: 5. Theoretically, the void ratio in soils can have the following values
explain: While void ratios can technically exceed 1 in organic soils or soft clays, for typical theoretical soil models, it is often discussed in terms of being less than 1 or within specific ranges. Note: The answer key specifies 'b'.

q: 6. The water content of soils can be accurately determined by .............
explain: Oven drying at 105-110°C is the standard reference method for accurate water content determination.

q: 7. The functional equation for specific gravity (G) water content (w), void ratio (e) and degree of saturation (Sr) is
explain: The fundamental soil mechanic relation is Se = wG. Rearranging for e gives e = wG/S.

q: 8. The ratio of the difference between the void ratio of the soil in its loosest and fully dense state is termed as
explain: These terms—relative density and density index—are used interchangeably to describe how dense a soil is relative to its limits.

q: 9. The percentage of the porosity of loose sand is in the range of
explain: Loose sands have higher void spaces, typically resulting in porosity between 40% and 50%.

q: 10. Which method is quickest to find the water content of soils
explain: The calcium carbide method provides rapid results (minutes) compared to the standard 24-hour oven-drying method.

q: 11. The maximum water content at which a reduction in water content does not cause a decrease in volume of soil mass is known as
explain: The shrinkage limit is the water content below which the soil volume remains constant even if the soil is dried further.

q: 12. Saturated clay test for shear strength can be performed by
explain: For saturated clay, the unconfined compression test directly gives the undrained shear strength without needing confining pressure, making it the simplest suitable test.

q: 13. The maximum compaction for any given water content corresponds to a per cent air-voids equal to .............
explain: Maximum theoretical compaction (the zero air voids line) corresponds to 0% air voids for a given water content.

q: 14. Three phase system is concerned with
explain: A three-phase system (solids + water + air) exists only in partially saturated soil, where both water and air occupy the voids.

q: 15. The relation between dry density, (γd), bulk density, (γ) and water content (w) is
explain: Dry density γd = γ/(1+w), derived from the definitions of bulk density and water content, since dry weight = total weight/(1+w).

q: 16. The relationship between void ratio (e) and porosity ratio (n) is
explain: Since n = e/(1+e), solving for e gives e = n/(1-n); the book's answer key lists option (c) as correct among the given (partly duplicated/typo) choices.

q: 17. For a cohesive soil, the modulus of elasticity .............
explain: Cohesive soils derive stiffness mainly from cohesion rather than confining pressure, so their modulus of elasticity is roughly constant with depth.

q: 18. The maximum dry density occurs at a particular water content which is known as
explain: In a compaction (Proctor) curve, the peak dry density occurs at the optimum moisture content (OMC).

q: 19. The ratio of total weight of saturated soil to its total volume is called .............
explain: Saturated unit weight is the total weight of soil (solids plus water filling all voids) per unit total volume.

q: 20. Theoretically, the void ratio in a soil can have a value of .............
options: can be less (or) more than one
explain: Depending on packing arrangement and soil type, void ratio can be less than, equal to, or greater than one.

q: 21. Equation for bulk unit weight γ in terms of specific gravity G, specific weight of water γw, voids ratio e, and degree of saturation S is written as
explain: The standard phase relationship gives bulk unit weight γ = γw(G+eS)/(1+e), combining the weight of solids and water per unit total volume.

q: 22. The minimum water content at which the soil just begins to crumble when rolled into threads 3 mm in diameter is known as .............
explain: This is the standard definition of the plastic limit, determined by the thread-rolling test.

q: 23. The minimum water content at which the soil just begins to crumble when rolled into threads 3 mm in diameter, is known
explain: This is the classic Atterberg definition of the plastic limit test procedure (rolling a 3 mm thread until it crumbles).

q: 24. Through a point in a loaded soil, the normal stress is maximum on .............
options: plane making an angle of 45 with principal planes
explain: By definition, principal planes carry zero shear, and the major principal plane carries the maximum normal stress.

q: 25. The bearing capacity of a strip footing on a saturated clay is 120 kN/m². The bearing capacity of a circular footing (diameter = width) will be
explain: For saturated clay (φ=0 condition), the shape factor increases bearing capacity for circular/square footings compared to a strip footing (Nc for circular > Nc for strip), so it will be more than 120 kN/m².

q: 26. The curve showing the relationship between the dry unit weight and the water content of a soil for a given compactive effort, is called
explain: This is precisely the definition of the compaction (moisture-density) curve obtained from a Proctor test.

q: 27. Out of the following, which will have the maximum value of surface tension force .............
explain: Mercury has an exceptionally high surface tension compared to typical liquids like water, petrol, or acetone.

q: 28. The value of cohesion of a saturated clay will be ............. times the value of unconfined compression strength
explain: For saturated clay under undrained conditions, cohesion c = qu/2, i.e. half the unconfined compressive strength.

q: 29. Ratio of weight of water to weight of solids in a given soil is
explain: This is the standard definition of water content, w = Ww/Ws.

q: 30. The trace moisture absorbed by a dry soil form the atmosphere is called .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'none of the above'; the standard geotechnical term for this trace absorbed moisture is actually hygroscopic moisture.

q: 31. Percentage air voids and porosity are related by .............
explain: Percentage air voids equals porosity times air content: na = n x ac.

q: 32. The ratio of the volume of voids to the total volume of soil mass is called .............
explain: Porosity is defined as the ratio of void volume to the total volume of the soil mass.

q: 33. A clay deposit which is not fully consolidated under the existing over burden pressure is known as .............
explain: A deposit still consolidating under its current overburden (excess pore pressure not fully dissipated) is termed under-consolidated.
